title: AcceptDialog's buttons position not consistent
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: v4.5.dev5.official [64b09905c], v4.4.1.stable.mono.official [49a5bc7b6], v4.3.stable.mono.official [77dcf97d8], v4.2.2.stable.official [15073afe3], v4.2.1.stable.official [b09f793f5]

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable.mono - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3060 (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.6636) - AMD Ryzen 7 3700X 8-Core Processor (16 threads)

### Issue description

AcceptDialog's buttons position is not always centered while the OK button is hidden. Here's the code attached to an AcceptDialog and the correspoding results:
### **Example 1** 
```gdscript
extends AcceptDialog

var confirmButton : Button
var cancelButton : Button

func _ready() -> void:
	get_ok_button().hide()
	cancelButton = add_cancel_button("Cancel")
	confirmButton = add_button("Confirm", true)
```
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f60de1cf-658d-44e6-8c01-f78ad0a9da01)

Other combinations creates different results. Removing the 'right' flag fixes the issues, but obviously swaps the buttons.

### **Example 2** 
```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	get_ok_button().hide()
	cancelButton = add_cancel_button("Cancel")
	confirmButton = add_button("Confirm")
```
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/65e0e116-618e-4fb9-90f8-6d5194004287)


Another solution is to substitute the cancel button with a custom one.

### **Example 3** 
```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	get_ok_button().hide()
        confirmButton = add_button("Confirm", true)
	cancelButton = add_button("Cancel")
```
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1939605b-25d6-4a8a-a43d-6475bd2c0880)

But again, removing the 'right' flag modify the behavior and uncenter them.

### **Example 4** 
```gdscript
func _ready() -> void:
	get_ok_button().hide()
	confirmButton = add_button("Confirm")
	cancelButton = add_button("Cancel")
```
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/81069aef-048d-460e-a89d-7f535bd4ea7f)


Here's a final comparison with the OK button not hidden for example 1 and 4. My guess is that the OK button doesn't hide correctly and still occupy a space in the button row with zero width. 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0f0ffcfd-61b5-41c4-a1d7-b750a809e62b)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/c7db047b-ace5-4d87-b10c-ee20ac05e2b9)


![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/9ff98a3a-82ca-45ac-bb36-a25806c1506c)
![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ff835a18-fe08-4f81-bf89-79e099ab3beb)

The second and third examples kind of works because the hidden OK button is in the middle and doesn't break the simmetry, but it creates a larger gap. Of couse it's not an engine breaking issue the behavior across buttons in the AcceptDialog is not consistent.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a control scene
2. Add a AcceptDialog
3. Attach a script
4. Hide the OK button
5. Add a cancel button
6. Add a custom button with flag 'right' set to true

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

MRP of the v4.4.1.stable.mono.official [49a5bc7b6] version

[MRP.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/20643636/MRP.zip)
